summary: Grays Harbor Co., WA: 1934 cab, WWII Aircraft Warning Service station, 1957 timber tower; tower removed 1972-73 (sources differ); cab footings remain below summit.

facts.design: 14x14-foot cab (1934); a 40-foot treated timber R-6 tower (1957, per register and Firelookout.com); an 8x16-foot AWS cabin added 1944
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1972 or 1973 (sources differ). The register says one removal attempt ended with it sinking in Lake Quinault; WillhiteWeb gives a second account. Cabin footings reportedly remain on the hillside below the summit.

staffing.status: Aircraft Warning Service observers during WWII; no later staffing in the sources read

access.note: Olympic National Forest land reached by gravel road and a trail from a trailhead, per WillhiteWeb's trip report. No closure is mentioned in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: Gravel roads to a trailhead, then about half a mile to the summit with a 272-foot gain (WillhiteWeb). Part of the drive runs along the boundary with Quinault Tribe land.

events.note: 14x14-foot cab: register and Firelookout.com give 1934; WillhiteWeb says 1932 or 1934
Panoramic photos taken from the cab roof on June 15, 1935 by George Clisby
Olympia Filter Center activated the site on March 10, 1942 as Aircraft Warning Service station Baker 7-3
8x16-foot cabin added for year-round living, per the May 1, 1944 AWS station report as quoted by Forest Lookouts
40-foot treated timber R-6 tower replaced the cab per the register and Firelookout.com. WillhiteWeb gives 1964 for a rebuilt wooden tower.
WillhiteWeb: lookout rebuilt on a wooden tower. Conflicts with the 1957 date.
WillhiteWeb: no longer needed and removed by helicopter in 1973
Radio reflector equipment on the summit removed
Registered January 13, 2012 as US 1185, WA 86; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Firelookout.com give 1934 for the 14x14 cab; WillhiteWeb says 1932 or 1934. The story uses 1934 and notes the hedge.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: (1) the tower's date: 1957 (register, Firelookout.com, WillhiteWeb's second source) vs 1964 (WillhiteWeb's main account). (2) Removal year: gone by 1972 (register, Firelookout.com) vs removed by helicopter in 1973 (WillhiteWeb). (3) Fate of the tower: lake sinking (register, Firelookout.com, WillhiteWeb's first source) vs reuse at the Snohomish County Airport (WillhiteWeb's second source). Story reports all three. The 1957 tower height of 12.2 m is converted from the register's 40 feet. The 'public' access level is inferred from National Forest land and trailhead parking in an undated trip report; the story omits directions. The Forest Lookouts page quotes the AWS station report of May 1, 1944 but the page was not read in original form.
